description: Propose a Panel from candidate ids of an open page. Banquish confirms it on the page, which the first Panel from it takes over as its own. The page stays open to you for more Panels: its ids stay valid for expand, find, add_panel and update_panel, and each further Panel gets a fresh copy of the page, where Banquish replays your reveals and finds the parts again, which takes a few seconds (refused if they aren't found). reveal and screenshot need the page opened again once a Panel has taken it. Each id is one part; several ids make one Composite Panel, for parts of the page that act on each other (a player and its transcript, a chart and its time picker): they show together in one tile and stay live together. exclude takes ids of candidates inside the chosen parts that the Panel leaves out (an ad, a reply box, the rest of a container whose text you want); any other id is refused with the reason. Mode is "item" (follow this specific thing, the default) or "spot" (whatever occupies this place). Placement is where its Tile goes on the Workspace's grid, as in arrange; without one it goes full width below the last Tile. With h, a Panel's Tile is that tall where its Panel is taller, and its Panel scrolls inside it; h beyond its Panel's own height is capped at that height, and the Fit report says so (capped). Returns the Fit report: at the user's window, which Tiles are scaled below their Panel's minimum width, have an h taller than their Panel (capped, with the h they got), scroll inside, fell back to crop, are broken or ambiguous, or leave their Tile's width unused, and any gaps between Tiles. A Tile whose page hasn't laid it out at its width yet (one not on screen, say) is settling: a later report says how it fits. While a settling Tile's minimum width isn't known, whether the Workspace shows as one column isn't either: oneColumn is left out, and the summary says so.
name: add_panel
